name: CIG Raton Basin 2010 Expansion

values.OtherEnglishNames: CIG Raton Basin 2010 Expansion; North Raton Lateral
values.EndLocation: CIG mainline interconnect, El Paso County

researcher_notes: The project is a new 16 inch pipeline, not compression, built by Colorado Interstate Gas Company under FERC docket CP09-464. A Federal Register notice of the application, dated 30 September 2009, describes the Raton 2010 Expansion Project, also called the North Raton Lateral, as about 118.6 miles of 16 inch pipe in Las Animas, Huerfano, Pueblo and El Paso counties, Colorado, with about 130,000 dekatherms per day of capacity and an estimated cost of about $132 million. The Energy Information Administration project list (August 2026 release, Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 672) records 118 miles, 16 inches, 130 million cubic feet per day, a cost of 132 million dollars, status completed, in service 18 November 2010. Length is staged as 118 miles, the figure both sources give. The Colorado Interstate Gas system already has a row, P0168, but it is a 6,920 km whole-system row with no segment name, and this is a distinct new line of more than 25 km, so it needs its own expansion row under the parent name. Owner and parent follow P0168. The two sources are independent origins only in part: the notice is a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission document and the project list is a federal energy statistics release that tracks it. No route was found; the Colorado Interstate Gas filing maps were not searched, so a route is still owed. The Federal Register page is read through a Cloudflare clearance. Confidence is high for the values and medium on independence.
